comments.author: satvikberi
comments.text:
I'm very curious if anyone has a somewhat detailed, non-hype account of finding more than two Claude Code instances at a time useful. Personally, I use one most of the time, and two occasionally when I have some long-running background process, but I've yet to find a case for three.

The only one I know of is Chris Rackaukas, who mentions it being useful for lots of boilerplate updating of a large number of open source repos: https://www.stochasticlifestyle.com/claude-code-in-scientific-computing-experiences-maintaining-julias-sciml-infrastructure/

comments.author: steveklabnik
comments.text:
I tap out at 3 Claudes at a time.

That’s about how many it takes for me to be basically done reviewing one and kicking off another task before another needs my attention for whatever reason.

comments.author: Student
comments.text: Yeah I can only assume that people who use more have figured out how to get the agent to spend a long time looping against some objective function.

comments.text:
I’ve had multiple sessions working on different things or two working on the same task in parallel on different worktrees to allow me to compare and contrast.
